title: The Case of the Silent Bell
story: On the Sunday before Thanksgiving, the bell ringer at St. Brendan's heaved on the rope and got nothing but a soft thump: someone had wrapped the clapper in a wool scarf. The tower sign-in sheet (Hattie's idea, naturally) lists five climbers that week, each on a different weekday, each with a different scarf and a different reason. The scarf on the clapper is cable-knit. Who muffled the bell?

texts: The climber in the striped scarf went up exactly 3 days after the climber with the view in mind.
Tova did not go up with the view in mind.
The climber with pigeons in mind wore either the plaid or the cable scarf.
Linus went up on either Monday or Tuesday.
The climber with dusting in mind went up on either Tuesday or Thursday.
The climber in the cable scarf did not go up with bats in mind.
Linus did not go up with pigeons in mind.
Hattie went up with either repairs or dusting in mind.
The climber with repairs in mind is either Tova or Pablo.
Gideon went up on either Thursday or Friday.
Of the climber with the view in mind and the climber with pigeons in mind, one wore the plaid scarf and the other wore the argyle scarf.
Of the climber with bats in mind and the climber with pigeons in mind, one is Linus and the other is Gideon.
